verdicts.note: One-term incumbent with prior Lakewood council and charter-review service, running on her first-term record and 'two decades of public service and executive management experience' [S1][S2][S6]. Several sources repeat this, so high holds; one term keeps it at -1.

Public dashboards, open data and cost reduction 'from process, not headcount' [S1], plus 'the highest level of service possible at the lowest burden to taxpayers' and 'fiscal responsibility' in his statement [S7]. That is the audit-and-restrain pole, applied to the office's own operations. Medium holds.

Never held elected office and says office 'should be about serving residents, not political ambition or the next position' [S7], against a sitting incumbent. His case also rests on five years as county elections supervisor and statewide election-system work [S1][S7], so +1 rather than +2.

The score rests on affiliation: his Cascade Party board seat [S1]. Disclosing that membership is transparency about himself, not a position on PAC money, term limits, dark money, RCV or direct democracy, the pole-B markers, and the basis admits he states none. The new-county effort is about service geography. Scoring party membership is the inference-from-affiliation the rules exclude; drop it (it is low and outside the alignment math either way).
